title: SAGA: Scene-Aware, Goal-Evolving Agents for Long-Horizon CivRealm Strategy Planning
title_zh: SAGA：面向长程 CivRealm 策略规划的场景感知、目标演化智能体
abstract_en: Long-horizon strategic planning in complex strategy games demands concurrent reasoning across multiple decision domains under imperfect information and sparse reward. Existing LLM-based agents suffer from three systematic failures: scene blindness from raw tile coordinates, context overflow and domain coupling from monolithic state dumps, and shallow cross-game learning that treats each episode in isolation. We present SAGA, an LLM multi-agent framework with three mechanisms each directly targeting one class of failure: (i) a Map-Semantic Scene Graph that encodes typed spatial relations among game entities into per-unit natural-language context, resolving spatial blindness without global token inflation; (ii) a Tool-Augmented Planner that pulls fine-grained domain state on demand and dispatches per-domain directives to dedicated specialist controllers, eliminating context overflow, domain coupling, and mechanical constraint violations; and (iii) a Dual-Horizon Feedback Loop that combines periodic within-game goal generation with structured cross-game causal post-mortem, enabling principled strategic evolution without manual reward engineering. Evaluated on FreeCiv, SAGA attains the highest mean civilization score -- the environment's sole sparse objective reward -- with lower variance than the two strongest baselines, and is the only method that significantly surpasses every baseline on infrastructure construction, the resource axis most readily sacrificed under multi-objective conflict. It outscores the two strongest baselines in most head-to-head games while cutting output tokens (the dominant decoding cost) by 27%. Equipped with the cross-game evolution module, SAGA reaches the highest end-of-chain score across five successive episodes. Ablation studies confirm that each architectural component contributes independently to this advantage.
abstract_zh: 本文提出 SAGA，一个用于复杂策略游戏长程规划的 LLM 多智能体框架，面向不完美信息、稀疏奖励和多决策域并行推理场景。针对现有 LLM 智能体的三类系统性问题——基于原始地图坐标导致的场景盲视、单体状态输入造成的上下文溢出与决策域耦合、以及跨局经验学习浅层化——SAGA 设计了三项机制：Map-Semantic Scene Graph 将游戏实体间的类型化空间关系编码为面向单元的自然语言上下文；Tool-Augmented Planner 按需拉取细粒度领域状态，并将指令分发给专门控制器；Dual-Horizon Feedback Loop 结合局内周期性目标生成与跨局结构化因果复盘，实现策略演化。FreeCiv 实验显示，SAGA 在平均文明分数这一稀疏目标奖励上取得最高成绩且方差更低，在基础设施建设这一资源维度上显著超过所有基线，并在多数两两对战中优于最强基线，同时输出 token 成本降低 27%。跨局演化模块使其在连续五局中达到最高最终得分，消融实验证明各组件均有独立贡献。
key_points_zh: SAGA 面向 FreeCiv/CivRealm 长程策略规划，解决 LLM agent 在复杂策略游戏中的空间理解、上下文管理和跨局学习问题。
Map-Semantic Scene Graph 将地图实体及其空间关系转化为单元级自然语言上下文，避免直接依赖原始 tile 坐标造成的场景盲视，同时控制 token 增长。
Tool-Augmented Planner 通过按需调用工具获取领域状态，并将军事、城市、科研等任务交给专门 controller，减少上下文溢出、领域耦合和非法操作。
Dual-Horizon Feedback Loop 同时进行局内目标更新和跨局因果复盘，使智能体能在无需手工奖励设计的情况下持续改进战略。
实验表明 SAGA 在平均 civilization score、基础设施建设、head-to-head 胜率和连续多局演化表现上优于主要基线，并将输出 token 成本降低 27%。

llm_assessment.comment: Useful long-horizon game-agent architecture with feedback loops, but its value is tied to a specific strategy-game environment.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 该工作提出了有用的长程游戏智能体架构和反馈循环，但价值较依赖特定策略游戏环境。
